- If sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33) or oscillating, model underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is near support.
- After a sharp spike in price or sentiment, model often overshoots and fails to correct — apply a “cool-down” rule: reduce forecast by 5–10% after peak.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias — if forecast is trending sharply upward, check if sentiment is weakening; if so, reverse direction or flatten slope.
- Forecast horizon 30d often misses early breakout phases — if sentiment turns bullish sharply, model lags; adjust forecast to align with sentiment shift within 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model tends to average out — avoid linear extrapolation; use sentiment-weighted smoothing or adaptive decay.
